title: TennisExplore chunk record
description: The retrieval contract (TENISE-15 / E3-09). One object per indexed chunk. Version 2 makes acl_groups, event_date and authors mandatory and enforced at ingest, because adding an indexed field after the corpus is embedded means re-embedding all of it.

chunk_id.description: Stable unique id, doc_id#pNNNN. Citations resolve through this, so it must not change between rebuilds of the same document.

doc_id.description: The document this chunk came from. Used to group citations and to promote sibling chunks.

modality.description: document = prose, record = a verbalised row of structured data, media = a transcript or frame description. One index holds all three; this field is what lets a single query rank a research passage and a match row together.

source_type.description: research_paper, match_report, ranking_data, policy, etc. Mirrors SOURCE_TYPES in shared/constants.

provenance.description: Where the file came from. Needed to keep synthetic demo data out of any evaluation that claims to measure real performance.

section.description: Heading the chunk sits under, when we could detect one. Feeds the contextual header.

text.description: The chunk body as indexed, WITHOUT the contextual header. Kept clean so a citation quotes what the document actually says.

context_header.description: The situating prefix that was prepended before embedding and before BM25 tokenisation. Stored separately so you can see exactly what the model saw.

embedding_text.description: Exactly what went into the embedding model: context_header + text. Stored for reproducibility -- if a rebuild produces different vectors, this is how you find out why.

acl_groups.description: MANDATORY. Flattened domain:sensitivity:program grant strings. Enforced before fusion on both retrieval arms. A chunk with an empty list is treated as unreachable, never as public.

program.description: Which program owns the document, or * for documents that belong to none (research, policy).

authors.description: MANDATORY (may be empty). Who wrote it. Present so an answer can say who claimed something, and so the corpus can be filtered to a named researcher.

event_date.description: MANDATORY key (value may be null). ISO yyyy-mm-dd. The date the content is ABOUT -- publication date for a paper, match date for a record. Not the ingest date. Recency filtering and 'what happened in November' questions both need this.

ingested_at.description: When we processed it. Separate from event_date on purpose: they answer different questions.

source_uri.description: Absolute path or URI of the originating file. Not searchable, used to open the source from a citation.

entity_ids.description: Player ids, tournament ids and other exact handles pulled out of the text. BM25 already matches these, but keeping them explicit lets the router detect an entity lookup.
